title: Raise the foundation codec's 512-item ceiling for byte-typed arrays
description:
Filed by governor-7610ed5a (standing authority) from worker-f144c751's measured report (msg-b7275c46, 04:02Z) — do not re-derive.

THE BOUND: `MAX_ITEMS = 512` at apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-codec.ts:13 bounds `binding.exactBytes`, so the foundation context-manifest codec (task-3e891741's deliverable) refuses any context manifest over 512 rendered bytes — measured: 513 bytes → FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_MALFORMED. Real agent contexts are thousands of bytes.

WHY FILED: the bound is INVISIBLE to every gate — the codec suite is green (fixtures render ~70 bytes), daemon suite 130 files / 2799 tests green. Nothing reds until task-22fa35a5 (ledger writer) feeds a realistic manifest, at which point it presents as a defect in the ledger writer rather than an inherited bound in a shared helper. Same shape as the unrostered-boundary class: a real constraint no gate reports, landing on whoever touches it next.

SCOPE (worker's suggestion, architect decides): own foundation-attempt-codec.ts; either raise MAX_ITEMS for byte-typed arrays specifically or give the shared snapshot helper a bytes-aware path. The DoD must include a test sealing a manifest at REALISTIC size (thousands of bytes) through the real codec. CAUTION: the helper is SHARED with the attempt codec — the attempt-codec suite must stay green under the change, and the bound exists as a hostile-input defense, so the widened path must remain bounded (a larger explicit cap or per-type cap, not unbounded).

SEQUENCING: task-22fa35a5 (Commit the Foundation context manifest before launch) hard-hits this first — its planner should treat this task as a dependency or absorb it with an explicit scope note.
definitionOfDone: A context manifest of realistic size (≥4KB rendered bytes) seals and re-admits through the production codec round-trip with digest match
byte-typed array bounds remain explicit and finite — the hostile oversized-input case still refuses with its exact code
The shared attempt-codec suite and the context-manifest codec suite are both green under the change, run as separate legs with printed nonzero counts
A mutation drill removing the new bound (or restoring the old 512 cap) reddens a NAMED test each way

comments.content: CURRENT-BYTE AUDIT (HEAD moved through d60a48f while peers worked): defect reproduced through real @moe/context selectContext -> renderContext -> production codec: a 4KiB context renders >4KiB exactBytes and refuses FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_MALFORMED@FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_CODEC. Safe route after prerequisite task-3e891741bef14097bbed6d820b392f98 is DONE: keep generic MAX_ITEMS=512; add an exact-path, descriptor-safe 64KiB byte-vector snapshot allowance only for manifest.binding.exactBytes; wire only the two context-codec snapshot calls; add a focused attempt-codec suite pinning unconfigured 513-item byte-looking arrays still refuse REQUEST_MALFORMED@DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT; extend the real context roundtrip/64KiB+1 exact-refusal tests. Conditional ownership is four paths: foundation-attempt-codec.ts, foundation-context-manifest-codec.ts, new foundation-attempt-codec.test.ts, foundation-context-manifest-codec.test.ts. task-22fa35a59f204777b4db56f7516ef57b is the named consumer and has been warned it must wait on this task.

blockedReason: BLOCKED ON ACTIVE PRODUCER OWNERSHIP, not technical design. task-3e891741bef14097bbed6d820b392f98 is reopened WORKING after QA rejection and owns foundation-context-manifest-codec.ts plus its focused test; the safe path-scoped byte-vector fix must edit both, so submitting/starting 5d now would collide with an in-flight owner. The conditional four-file plan and current-byte reproduction are recorded in comment-e91831f44065476eaf27ecaef325ccf9. Once 3e is DONE, re-plan 5d with the exact-path 64KiB byte-array allowance while preserving generic MAX_ITEMS=512. Consumer task-22fa35a59f204777b4db56f7516ef57b has been notified to wait.
